playbook:
When I'm in a build phase and I can afford a settlement (1 wood, 1 brick, 1 grain, 1 ore), I build the settlement rather than a road.

When I can afford a settlement I do not post trades that would give away any resource needed for that settlement.

When I cannot afford a settlement but can afford a road (1 wood + 1 brick), I build a road only if it meaningfully changes scoring this turn or is strategically necessary; otherwise I save resources for a future settlement.

When I need a single specific resource to complete a settlement or road, I post a one-for-one offer to a player who demonstrably holds that resource this round, offering a resource of roughly equal immediate value (examples: ore for wood, grain for wood). I always name a real resource and a single counterparty who currently has that resource.

When I post an offer I prefer to keep ore and other settlement-critical resources unless the offered resource is genuinely expendable for the same-turn or clearly faster path to a settlement.

When I am offered a trade, I accept it only if:
- it does not prevent me from making an immediate higher-value build I can already afford (e.g., I would not trade away a needed resource if I can already build a settlement), and
- it meaningfully advances my scoring path (e.g., completes a settlement) or is strictly neutral for my ability to build next turn.
I also decline trades that would give an opponent the resource they need to overtake me on the same turn.

In the final round(s) when I am leading, I generally avoid posting offers and avoid accepting trades that could give opponents the resources to overtake me. I will only post or accept trades in the final round if the trade immediately completes my settlement/road this turn (i.e., guarantees my scoring improvement) and does not enable an opponent to beat me.

When a proposed trade would leave me with fewer moves toward my next settlement than before the trade, I decline it.

Do not post gratuitous trades when I already can build a settlement that turn — immediate +3 points is usually preferable to speculative future gain.

Avoid trades that are clearly generous to an opponent who is one build away from overtaking me; prefer offers that are reciprocal and consistent with both my immediate needs and protection of my lead.

1.text:
When I start a round and my holdings already meet a settlement cost, I build the settlement immediately rather than trading for marginal upside.

When I need one resource to complete a settlement and another player has repeatedly traded that resource for ore, I will post an offer of 1 ore for 1 of that resource to the specific player who has shown that pattern.

When an offer to me gives the single resource I need to finish a settlement and I can spare the requested resource without dropping below my ore threshold for future city/dev plans (default threshold = 3 ore), I accept it.

When an incoming offer would drop my ore below my city/dev threshold and the gain is only one resource that does not immediately convert into a settlement or a higher-scoring build this round, I decline.

When I cannot build a settlement this turn but can build a road with available wood+brick, I build the road to take the guaranteed 1 point rather than holding resources idle (unless holding enables a settlement next turn with high probability).

When I have enough ore to consider city/dev plans, I prioritize keeping ore over taking small single-resource trades unless the trade directly enables a 3-point settlement that I can build that round.

When posting an offer, I name a specific counterparty who has previously shown a propensity to accept that swap pattern rather than broadcasting a generic offer.

When multiple offers are posted to me, I accept any that immediately yield a buildable settlement or that leave my strategic resource thresholds intact; otherwise I accept none.

Do not trade away the single resource that is the bottleneck for a settlement if I can instead post an offer to acquire that bottleneck from the player who trades it most often.

If I lack both wood and grain (or another pair) so that no build is possible this round, avoid desperate unfavorable trades just to change holdings; instead wait to convert into a road or settlement on a later round when feasible.

If two or more players post identical offers (e.g., 1 grain for 1 wood) and I only need one of those resources to complete a settlement, prefer accepting from the counterparty who leaves me with better remaining resource balance or who has historically provided favorable trades.

If accepting a trade would convert a current build opportunity (settlement) into a non-build round, prefer declining unless the trade creates a guaranteed higher-point outcome this round.

2.text:
When I can afford a settlement, I build it immediately (use 1 wood, 1 brick, 1 grain, 1 ore) to maximize points now.

When I cannot build a settlement but can build a road with a single trade’s worth of resources, I prioritize acquiring the single missing wood or brick to make that road (1 wood + 1 brick → 1 point).

When I lack exactly one resource (wood, brick, or ore) that would enable an immediate settlement or road, I post one offer asking for that resource, offering 1 grain first, then 1 ore if grain is not available or is too valuable to keep (post: to Pk, give 1 grain, get 1 wood/brick/ore).

Do not post a trade if I already have the exact resources to build the highest-scoring available structure (no trade when a settlement is affordable).

Never post or accept a trade that would leave me with negative holdings of any resource at the start of the subsequent building phase; avoid trades that rely on receiving multiple resources across rounds or that assume other trades will cover shortages. Only make trades that settle against the holdings recorded at the start of the trading phase.

Do not trade away my last unit of a flexible building resource (especially wood or brick) unless the incoming resource enables an immediate build that yields equal or greater points.

When I have multiple offers available, accept any that independently enable an immediate build this round; otherwise accept none.

Avoid posting trades that will directly enable an opponent’s immediate high-value build (settlement or multiple points) unless the return gives me an immediate build worth at least as much.

If I have several grains but am chronically missing wood/brick, prioritize converting grain into those missing building materials earlier rather than hoarding grain for a future settlement. However, preserve enough grain to be able to trade for the single resource I most often need next turn.

When opponents repeatedly trade one resource type (e.g., grain) for another (e.g., ore or wood), exploit that pattern by offering the resource they’ve been giving up to get the resource I need, but still respect the “do not leave myself negative” rule.

If one resource alone blocks a build and I can get it via a single 1-for-1 trade at reasonable likelihood, make that offer; if completion requires multiple trades across rounds and would expose me to being unable to build, prefer to wait or seek a different partner/resource.

When I have neither wood nor brick and no simple single-trade path to either, do not post offers that give opponents what they need for immediate points unless the trade returns enable me to score immediately or block a larger opponent lead.

When offered a trade, accept it if it directly completes a build this round or strongly guarantees one next round without leaving me resource-starved; decline if it trades away a scarce flexible resource for something that won’t enable immediate scoring.

If midgame shows that hoarding grain alone fails to convert into wins, shift earlier to trading grain for missing building materials when the opportunity arises, while still following the conservative rule about not ending a trading phase with negative or critically low essential resources.
